payload.task_text:
Your research institution must establish comprehensive data archival and compliance procedures to ensure research data integrity and meets regulatory requirements. The first phase involves conducting a complete inventory of all research datasets and associated documentation. Identify all active research projects and their data files. Document dataset characteristics including file format, size, creation date, and data type. Organize documentation including study protocols, data collection procedures, and analytical methods. Create a centralized registry of all research datasets with essential metadata for each.

In the second phase, you will verify compliance of all datasets with applicable retention policies and funding agency requirements. Review institutional data retention policies specifying how long different data types must be retained. Check funding agency requirements including National Science Foundation, National Institutes of Health, and other sponsor mandates. Assess whether datasets meet funder requirements for data sharing and open access. Document any datasets with sensitive data requiring restricted access or deidentification. Verify that datasets include required documentation and metadata for reproducibility.

The third phase requires creating comprehensive archival metadata and preservation plans for each dataset. Develop standardized metadata documentation following relevant community standards for the research domain. Create detailed data dictionaries defining all variables and coding schemes. Document data provenance including collection methods, preprocessing steps, and quality assurance procedures. Create preservation plans addressing long-term storage, format migration, and access preservation for each dataset.

In the fourth phase, you will organize all research data in a compliant repository structure. Establish standardized directory hierarchies and naming conventions for all datasets. Ensure all files are in acceptable formats suitable for long-term preservation. Create backup copies of all datasets with off-site replication. Establish access controls ensuring appropriate security for sensitive data. Document all datasets in the institutional research data management system.

The fifth phase involves generating comprehensive compliance documentation. Create detailed archival plans for each dataset documenting retention requirements and preservation procedures. Verify that all documentation required by funders is complete and properly organized. Generate compliance checklists for each funding source. Create institutional compliance certifications confirming that data meets all applicable requirements.

The sixth phase requires finalizing archival and communicating with stakeholders. Document all archival procedures and create training materials for researchers. Send compliance verification communications to institutional leadership and funding agencies. Store all archival documentation with version control in the institutional repository. Schedule meetings with research teams to confirm data organization and compliance with requirements.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly as the main agent without dispatching any sub-agents. The three task-provided datasets are small enough to inventory directly: in one native-parallel read-only batch, inspect these exact task-visible source objects — raw_datasets/NSF-2021-CLIM-001/{metadata.json,temperature_records.csv,study_protocol.txt}, raw_datasets/NIH-2022-HLTH-002/{metadata.json,patient_outcomes.csv,study_protocol.txt}, and raw_datasets/DOE-2023-ENRG-003/{metadata.json,measurements.csv,study_protocol.txt}. For each dataset freeze its exact project key, funder, PI, retention years, sensitivity, data file format/size/header/row count, protocol coverage, variable dictionary, provenance evidence, sharing/access constraints, documentation gaps, and preservation risks; treat unrelated top-level sample/config files as workspace context, not research datasets, and preserve every source unchanged. Then directly: create one explicit directory per frozen dataset with preservation copies of every mapped data/documentation file (originals untouched, workspace-only backups labeled as local simulations, and an off-site capability blocker recorded unless an authorized remote target is actually visible) plus the centralized dataset registry; create the compliance documentation package (archival plan, data dictionary, provenance/preservation/access procedure, sponsor checklist, researcher training guidance, version-control instructions, and a certification separating verified compliance from gaps) for every dataset and sponsor. Reconcile the three dataset keys across registry, copies and documents; resolve email recipients and meeting dates/times only from task-visible evidence, reporting the precise missing-parameter blocker instead of guessing, and complete the remaining side effects exactly once. Call claim_done; do not add a separate verification phase.

You are supporting a research data archival & compliance program at a research institution. Today's date: 2026-08-29. Workspace root: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-research-data-archival-compliance/workspace

Your job: produce the Phase 1 (centralized inventory/registry) and Phase 4 (compliant repository structure, backups, access controls, RDMS registration) artifacts. Write local files only. NEVER modify the source files under <root>/raw_datasets/ — only copy from them.

KNOWN FACTS (verified; do not re-derive):
Three active research datasets, source files at <root>/raw_datasets/<ID>/:

1. DOE-2023-ENRG-003 "Renewable Energy Adoption Study" — Funder: DOE (U.S. Dept of Energy); PI: Dr. Carol Wu; Retention: 5 years; Sensitive: No.
   - Data file: measurements.csv (1,462 bytes; CSV; columns site,date,energy_kwh; 65 rows; energy consumption in kWh from plants plant_0..plant_3, collected Feb 2024; quantitative time-series).
   - Docs: study_protocol.txt, metadata.json.
2. NIH-2022-HLTH-002 "Patient Outcomes Study" — Funder: NIH (National Institutes of Health); PI: Dr. Bob Chen; Retention: 10 years; Sensitive: YES (PHI — patient_id, outcome, followup_days; 40 patient records P0000–P0039; requires deidentification and restricted access).
   - Data file: patient_outcomes.csv (514 bytes; CSV; clinical outcomes data).
   - Docs: study_protocol.txt, metadata.json.
3. NSF-2021-CLIM-001 "Climate Variability Study" — Funder: NSF (National Science Foundation); PI: Dr. Alice Martinez; Retention: 7 years; Sensitive: No.
   - Data file: temperature_records.csv (1,218 bytes; CSV; columns date,site,temp_c; 50 rows; daily temperature °C from sites site_0..site_4, Jan 2024; environmental time-series).
   - Docs: study_protocol.txt, metadata.json.

For all three data files: filesystem created date = 2026-08-29, last modified = 2026-08-07. Data collection start: DOE 2024-02-01; NIH 2024 (patient follow-ups, project start 2022); NSF 2024-01-01.

DELIVERABLES (exact paths under the workspace root):

A. Centralized registry:
1. <root>/registry/research_data_registry.csv — one row per dataset with columns: dataset_id, project_title, pi, funder, data_files, file_formats, total_size_bytes, data_type, data_collection_start, file_created, file_last_modified, retention_years, sensitivity, access_control, archive_path, status.
2. <root>/registry/research_data_registry.json — same data as structured JSON (include per-file detail: file_name, format, size_bytes, description).
3. <root>/registry/research_data_registry.xlsx — try to create with Python (mcp__local__python_execute) using openpyxl; sheets: "Registry" (same as CSV) and one sheet per dataset listing its files. If openpyxl is unavailable, fall back to CSV+JSON only and note it in the report.
4. <root>/registry/dataset_inventory_report.md — Phase 1 report: methodology, inventory of active projects, per-dataset characteristics (format, size, creation date, data type), documentation inventory (study protocols, data collection procedures, metadata files present), summary table, and any observations (e.g., NIH dataset flagged sensitive).

B. Compliant repository structure:
5. <root>/repository/README.md — documented directory hierarchy standard and naming conventions (lowercase, underscores, dataset-id prefix, data/ vs documentation/ vs metadata/ subfolders, versioning suffix), plus format policy (CSV/JSON/TXT = preservation-friendly open formats).
6. For each dataset, <root>/repository/<DATASET_ID>/ containing:
   - README.md (dataset overview, PI, funder, retention, sensitivity, contents, access notes)
   - data/<original data file> (byte-identical copy via terminal `cp`)
   - documentation/study_protocol.txt and documentation/metadata.json (copies)
   Use canonical names; keep original filenames for traceability.
7. <root>/repository/backup/ — a backup copy of each dataset directory (data + documentation), plus <root>/repository/backup/BACKUP_MANIFEST.md documenting: backup contents, md5 checksums of each backed-up data file (compute with terminal `md5sum`), backup date 2026-08-29, and an off-site replication plan (encrypted off-site storage, quarterly sync cadence, disaster-recovery restore test annually, responsible party = Institutional IT / Research Data Office).
8. <root>/repository/access_controls.md — access control matrix: NIH-2022-HLTH-002 = RESTRICTED (role-based access, only PI + IRB-approved researchers, data use agreement, deidentification required, encryption at rest, no open sharing of raw PHI); DOE-2023-ENRG-003 and NSF-2021-CLIM-001 = OPEN (read access to research community, per funder open-access expectations). Include file permission recommendations (e.g., 640 for restricted, 644 for open).

C. RDMS registration:
9. <root>/registry/rdms_registration.md — documentation of each dataset registered in the institutional Research Data Management System: record IDs RDM-2026-001 (DOE), RDM-2026-002 (NIH), RDM-2026-003 (NSF), registration date 2026-08-29, registered fields (title, PI, funder, retention, sensitivity, repository path, backup status, access level, RDMS contact).

Use terminal (mcp__terminal__run_command) for cp/md5sum and Python (mcp__local__python_execute) for xlsx. Verify all deliverables exist at the end (e.g., directory tree or ls) and report the final paths, checksums, and any fallbacks used. Return a concise summary of what was created.
Build registry and repository structure

You are supporting a research data archival & compliance program at a research institution. Today's date: 2026-08-29. Workspace root: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-research-data-archival-compliance/workspace

Your job: produce the Phase 2 (compliance verification) and Phase 5 (compliance documentation: archival plans, funder checklists, certifications) artifacts. Write local files under <root>/compliance/. You may read the raw source files under <root>/raw_datasets/ if needed but do not modify them.

KNOWN FACTS (verified):
1. DOE-2023-ENRG-003 "Renewable Energy Adoption Study" — DOE; PI Dr. Carol Wu; retention 5 years; non-sensitive; data: measurements.csv (site,date,energy_kwh; kWh readings; Feb 2024); docs: study_protocol.txt, metadata.json.
2. NIH-2022-HLTH-002 "Patient Outcomes Study" — NIH; PI Dr. Bob Chen; retention 10 years; SENSITIVE (PHI — patient_id, outcome, followup_days; 40 records); docs present.
3. NSF-2021-CLIM-001 "Climate Variability Study" — NSF; PI Dr. Alice Martinez; retention 7 years; non-sensitive; data: temperature_records.csv (date,site,temp_c; Jan 2024); docs present.

FUNDER & POLICY REQUIREMENTS to incorporate (accurate summaries):
- Institutional retention policy (to be documented): general research data retained minimum 3 years after project completion; PHI/clinical data minimum 6 years (HIPAA record retention); in all cases at least the funder-required period (max of institutional vs funder). Datasets: DOE 5 yrs, NIH 10 yrs, NSF 7 yrs — all meet policy.
- NSF (PAPPG): Data Management Plan required at proposal; data shared no later than publication or end of award; records retained ≥3 years after closeout; metadata per community standards; open access expected.
- NIH (Data Management & Sharing Policy, effective 2023-01-25): DMS Plan required; scientific data shared no later than publication or end of award; data preserved ≥3 years after award end; sensitive/PHI data must be deidentified with restricted/controlled access (data use agreement); HIPAA compliance.
- DOE (DOE Public Access Plan, OSTI): data management & public access requirements; data shared in a timely manner; retention ≥3 years typical; DOE Order 241.1B.

DELIVERABLES (exact paths):
1. <root>/compliance/institutional_retention_policy.md — the institutional retention policy: purpose, scope, retention schedule by data type (raw data, processed data, PHI/clinical, publications/records), minimums, funder-requirement override rule, review/disposition process.
2. <root>/compliance/funder_requirements.md — detailed summary of NSF, NIH, DOE requirements (data management plans, sharing timelines, retention, open access, sensitive data handling, metadata/reproducibility expectations) plus a short section on other sponsor mandates (general federal research record requirements).
3. <root>/compliance/compliance_assessment.md — per-dataset compliance assessment: a comparison table (dataset, retention required vs policy, sharing/open-access status, sensitive data handling, reproducibility documentation, overall status) followed by narrative per dataset: (a) retention compliance — DOE 5yrs/NIH 10yrs/NSF 7yrs all meet/exceed policy; (b) funder sharing & open access — all meet sharing expectations; NIH requires controlled access + deidentification of PHI (raw patient_id should be pseudonymized in any public release); (c) sensitive data — NIH flagged, restricted access + encryption + DUA required; DOE/NSF open; (d) reproducibility — protocols and metadata.json present for all; note that analysis code/README are not yet present and recommend adding them (action item). Include overall findings, risk register, and recommendations.
4. <root>/compliance/archival_plans/DOE-2023-ENRG-003_archival_plan.md, <root>/compliance/archival_plans/NIH-2022-HLTH-002_archival_plan.md, <root>/compliance/archival_plans/NSF-2021-CLIM-001_archival_plan.md — per dataset: description, retention requirement & retention end date (compute: DOE ~2029, NIH ~2034, NSF ~2031 based on retention from data collection/project end), preservation procedures, storage locations, access controls, format considerations, review schedule, disposition/archival transfer steps, responsible parties.
5. <root>/compliance/checklists/compliance_checklist_NSF.md, <root>/compliance/checklists/compliance_checklist_NIH.md, <root>/compliance/checklists/compliance_checklist_DOE.md — funder-specific compliance checklists with checkbox items covering: data management plan, data sharing timeline, retention, metadata standards, sensitive data handling, reproducibility documentation, open access, certification. Mark each item as applicable/status for the relevant dataset(s) and include a checklist-completion section.
6. <root>/compliance/certifications/DOE-2023-ENRG-003_compliance_certification.md, <root>/compliance/certifications/NIH-2022-HLTH-002_compliance_certification.md, <root>/compliance/certifications/NSF-2021-CLIM-001_compliance_certification.md — institutional compliance certifications, one per dataset: statement of certification that the dataset meets institutional retention policy and funder (DOE/NIH/NSF) requirements for retention, sharing, sensitive data handling, and documentation; signed by the Institutional Research Data Officer; date 2026-08-29; include certification ID (e.g., CERT-2026-001/002/003).

Use accurate, professional institutional language. Verify files exist at the end and report the list of created paths with a one-line summary of each. Return a concise summary.
Build compliance assessments and certifications

You are supporting a research data archival & compliance program at a research institution. Today's date: 2026-08-29. Workspace root: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-research-data-archival-compliance/workspace

Your job: produce Phase 3 artifacts — standardized archival metadata, data dictionaries, provenance documentation, and preservation plans for each dataset. Write local files under <root>/metadata/. You may read raw source files under <root>/raw_datasets/ if needed (do not modify them).

KNOWN FACTS (verified):
1. DOE-2023-ENRG-003 "Renewable Energy Adoption Study" — DOE; PI Dr. Carol Wu; retention 5 years; non-sensitive. Data: measurements.csv — columns: site (plant_0..plant_3, categorical), date (YYYY-MM-DD), energy_kwh (numeric, kWh, energy consumption readings; 65 rows; Feb 2024). Docs: study_protocol.txt, metadata.json.
2. NIH-2022-HLTH-002 "Patient Outcomes Study" — NIH; PI Dr. Bob Chen; retention 10 years; SENSITIVE (PHI). Data: patient_outcomes.csv — columns: patient_id (P0000..P0039, pseudonymous identifier), outcome (0/1 binary), followup_days (numeric 30–69). 40 records. Docs: study_protocol.txt, metadata.json.
3. NSF-2021-CLIM-001 "Climate Variability Study" — NSF; PI Dr. Alice Martinez; retention 7 years; non-sensitive. Data: temperature_records.csv — columns: date (YYYY-MM-DD), site (site_0..site_4), temp_c (numeric °C). 50 rows; Jan 2024. Docs: study_protocol.txt, metadata.json.

METADATA STANDARDS to reference:
- Core standard: Dublin Core (title, creator, subject, description, publisher, contributor, date, type, format, identifier, source, language, relation, coverage, rights).
- Domain extensions: NSF climate dataset → ISO 19115 / ESIP / OGC geospatial metadata conventions; NIH health dataset → CDISC-style variable naming, HIPAA privacy considerations, DDI-style codebook; DOE energy dataset → DCAT-style dataset metadata. State the standard used in each metadata record.

DELIVERABLES (exact paths):
1. <root>/metadata/README.md — explains the metadata scheme: Dublin Core core + domain standards per dataset, file naming, how records map to the registry.
2. For EACH dataset, create directory <root>/metadata/<DATASET_ID>/ containing:
   a. metadata_record.json — standardized metadata record: Dublin Core fields (title, creator=PI, subject, description, publisher=Institution, contributor, date=2024 data collection, type=dataset, format=CSV, identifier=dataset ID, source=study protocol, language=en, relation=study protocol, coverage=time/space, rights=access level) plus domain-specific fields (spatial/temporal coverage, units, standard used, retention, sensitivity, access level, checksum placeholder note).
   b. data_dictionary.md — for every variable in the dataset's CSV: variable name, definition, data type, units, allowed values / coding scheme (e.g., outcome: 0=no event, 1=event; site codes), missing value convention, example. Also document the file structure and row count.
   c. provenance.md — data provenance: collection methods (instrumentation/sources: e.g., plant energy meters, clinical records extraction, temperature sensors/weather stations), preprocessing steps (cleaning, validation, formatting), quality assurance/QC procedures, data lineage, responsible personnel, date of collection (Feb 2024 / Jan 2024 / NIH patient follow-ups), any transformations.
   d. preservation_plan.md — per dataset preservation plan: long-term storage (institutional repository + backup/off-site replication), format migration strategy (CSV kept as open archival format; migration review trigger), access preservation (open vs restricted/controlled for NIH with deidentification and data use agreement), fixity/checksum verification schedule, review cadence (annual), retention period (5/10/7 years), disposition after retention, responsible roles.
3. <root>/metadata/INDEX.md — index linking each dataset to its metadata files.

Use professional archival terminology (OAIS concepts where appropriate: SIP/AIP/DIP, fixity). Verify all files exist at the end and report created paths. Return a concise summary.
Build metadata, dictionaries, preservation plans

You are supporting a research data archival & compliance program at a research institution. Today's date: 2026-08-29. Workspace root: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-research-data-archival-compliance/workspace

Do not modify anything outside that directory (other agents are writing to registry/, repository/, compliance/, metadata/ in parallel — leave them untouched).

CONTEXT (verified facts you may reference):
Three active datasets are being archived: DOE-2023-ENRG-003 (Renewable Energy Adoption Study, DOE, PI Dr. Carol Wu, 5-yr retention, non-sensitive), NIH-2022-HLTH-002 (Patient Outcomes Study, NIH, PI Dr. Bob Chen, 10-yr retention, SENSITIVE/PHI, restricted access + deidentification), NSF-2021-CLIM-001 (Climate Variability Study, NSF, PI Dr. Alice Martinez, 7-yr retention, non-sensitive). The archival program has: a centralized registry (registry/), a compliant repository (repository/ with data, documentation, backup/, access_controls.md), compliance documentation (compliance/ incl. archival plans, funder checklists, certifications), metadata records with data dictionaries, provenance and preservation plans (metadata/), and communications with stakeholders (emails to leadership & funders, meetings with research teams). Funder requirements: NSF PAPPG DMP & open sharing; NIH DMS Policy (2023) with controlled access for PHI; DOE Public Access Plan/OSTI.

DELIVERABLES (exact paths):
1. <root>/documentation/archival_procedures.md — comprehensive standard operating procedures for the institutional research data archival workflow: scope, roles & responsibilities (researcher/PI, Research Data Officer, IT), step-by-step procedures: (1) dataset intake & inventory, (2) metadata & data dictionary creation, (3) compliance verification (retention, funder requirements, sensitive data), (4) repository ingest (naming conventions, formats), (5) backup & off-site replication, (6) access control setup, (7) archival plan & certification, (8) periodic review & disposition. Include checklists and forms references.
2. <root>/documentation/training_materials.md — training materials for researchers: purpose of data archival & compliance, funder requirements at a glance (NSF/NIH/DOE), how to write data management plans, metadata and data dictionary guidance, sensitive data (PHI) handling & deidentification, how to submit data to the repository (step-by-step), common pitfalls, FAQ, and contact for support (Research Data Office).
3. <root>/documentation/version_control.md — version-control policy for all archival documentation: versioning scheme (semantic versioning MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH), changelog requirement, storage in the institutional version-controlled repository (git-based), commit conventions, review/approval workflow, retention of full history, and the initial version record (v1.0.0, dated 2026-08-29, initial archival program documentation).

Use clear, professional, institutional language. Verify the three files exist at the end and return a concise summary with the file paths.
Build archival procedures and training docs
